dialect: Latin American Spanish (broadly neutral, ustedes for plural 'you', no vosotros)

profile.grammar_notes: Two copulas: ser (identity, origin, time) and estar (location, temporary state); hay for existence. Subject pronouns usually dropped because verb endings mark the person; tú vs usted marks politeness (ustedes is the only plural 'you' in Latin America). Negation with no before the verb; double negatives (no… nada/nadie/nunca) are standard. Questions by intonation or question words with accents (qué, dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto, por qué). Want/can/must/go: querer, poder, tener que, ir a + infinitive (near future). Gustar construction (me gusta) reverses English subject/object. Preterite vs imperfect aspect contrast in the past. Closed sets: subject pronouns, object clitics, articles, question words, days, months, numbers.
